Tom — thanks, we can supply what you've listed. I'm attaching a boundary diagram and a CSV export of rotation schedule records (redacted where required).

High-level answers up front:
- Customer keys: BYOK supported via import (non-exportable keys) into FIPS-140-2/3 HSMs; customers can also opt for Redwood-managed KMS keys.
- HSM boundary: HSMs are hosted by our KMS vendor in dedicated FIPS-validated modules; the KMS cluster runs in our private subnet with strict egress rules.
- Rotation cadence: KEKs rotated annually by default; DEKs rotated on re-key events or quarterly for high-volume tenants. Last KEK rotation occurred 2028-11-18 (see CSV).
- In-transit: TLS 1.3 with ECDHE, cert rotation handled via automated CA renewals — we'll include the cert rotation runbook snippet.

See attached: sig-kms-hsm-boundary-v1.pdf, rotation-cadence-2024-2028.csv. Marissa — adding you to respond to the attestation/third-party bits.

Thanks,

Hi Tom — following up with the technical specifics you asked for. Quoting Jasmine's summary below for context.

On Tue, Jan 9, 2029 at 10:02 AM Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com> wrote:
> Tom — thanks, we can supply what you've listed. I'm attaching a boundary diagram and a CSV export of rotation schedule records (redacted where required).

Below are explicit answers tied to typical SIG control IDs:
- SIG/Crypt-2 (Key possession): For BYOK we import keys as non-exportable objects into the HSM; the private key material never leaves the HSM. Proof: HSM import logs + import job IDs (we can provide job IDs under NDA).
- SIG/Crypt-6 (Key rotation): KEK rotation performed by our KMS orchestration job (kms-rotate-kev) with deterministic versioning; DEK rotation is triggered by rekey policy or manually by tenant ops. Evidence attached: rotation-cadence-2024-2028.csv.
- SIG/Network-4 (In-transit): All external traffic uses TLS 1.3 + ECDHE; internal service-to-service uses mTLS with certs rotated every 90 days. Evidence: cert-rotation-runbook excerpt (we can circulate a sanitized snippet).
- HSM attestation: Our HSM vendor publishes FIPS/NIST attestations; we will attach the vendor attestation summary and provide contact/POC for full reports as needed.

Items we cannot share in-bundle: full HSM hardware serials and raw HSM audit logs (vendor confidentiality). We can provide hashed identifiers and signed attestation statements instead. If Acme needs a deeper review, we can schedule an NDA-covered audit with the vendor.

Action items:
- Jasmine: upload artifacts to the shared Drive link and notify Acme.
- Dylan: follow up to provide the job IDs for the KEK import and rotation events (redacted view).

—Marissa
